raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t run after every new idea. I do what I know, and I watch what the people around me do. This year I will still spread the risk. Cotton gives cash if the price is alright, maize is steady, and the vegetables bring money faster if they grow well. But my house only has 2 people, and I am 68, so I cannot manage too much fine work on every mu. I will keep fertilizer at a middling level, not too little, because if the crop goes yellow the loss is bigger than saving a few yuan. Since I have a well, I will irrigate when the ground turns dry, but I will not water too many times because pumping costs money. For the vegetable plots I will pay more attention, because cabbage and chili need closer care and can sell for better money. For maize and cotton I will keep things simpler and use the usual way.

For Chinese cabbage, I will put more land there because in our place it can sell well if the stand is even. I will use decent seed from the market, put base fertilizer first, then add more when it starts wrapping. For ordinary cabbage I will do a smaller area, same idea, because it needs labor and I cannot handle too much. Chili is troublesome but brings cash, so I will keep only a little. Cotton I will still plant because I have grown it many years and know how to manage it, but I won’t put too much land there since picking takes labor. Maize is the safest one, so I keep some land in it in case vegetable prices are bad.
